note: Step-by-step checklists for specific call tasks, in the order you'd do them. Each step is one action. 'source' quotes the PDS (checked word for word). 'member' adds a note when a loaded test member matches a condition (see src/members.js for condition names). 'form', 'rule' and 'calc' link to other parts of the companion.

items.title: Notice of intent to claim a tax deduction (NOI)
items.when: The member made personal (after-tax) contributions and wants to claim them as a tax deduction.

steps.do: Confirm which contributions: personal after-tax contributions the member paid into this UniSuper account, and the financial year they were made.

source.quote: then you may be eligible to claim a tax deduction on those contributions

steps.do: Check the money is still with UniSuper: not rolled out, withdrawn, or used to start a pension. If any of it has gone, the notice can't cover that part.

source.quote: In addition, UniSuper must still hold these contributions and can't have begun paying a superannuation income stream based on all or part of these contributions

member.text: {name} has a pension. Contributions used to start it can't be claimed.

steps.do: Check the deadline: the notice must be acknowledged before the member lodges that year's tax return, or by the end of the next financial year, whichever comes first.

source.quote: You must submit your claim (and we must acknowledge receipt in writing) before whichever of the following occurs first

steps.do: Ages 67 to 74: confirm the work test (40 hours within 30 consecutive days in the year of the contribution).

source.quote: Individuals aged 67-74 are required to meet the work test (or exemption) to claim a deduction on personal contributions.

member.text: {name} is {age}: the work test applies.

steps.do: Planning to split contributions with a spouse? Lodge the notice first, then the split.

source.quote: you must lodge the notice of your intention to claim a tax deduction with us before requesting that the contributions be split

steps.do: Planning to start a Retirement Phase or TTR pension? The notice must be lodged and acknowledged before the pension opens.

source.quote: before opening your Retirement Phase or TTR Flexi Pension account.

member.text: {name} is about to start a pension: lodge the notice now, before the pension application.

steps.do: Lodge it: online under Manage account, Notice of intent, or with the Notice of intent to claim or vary a tax deduction form.
Tell the member to wait for our written acknowledgement before claiming the deduction in their tax return.
Explain the effect: the amount claimed becomes a concessional contribution, taxed 15% in the fund, and counts towards the concessional cap.

source.quote: Any contributions on which you claim a tax deduction will be treated as concessional contributions

member.text: {name} has {ccUsed} of concessional contributions so far this year ({ccLeft} left under the cap before this claim).

mistakes: Rolling over, withdrawing or starting a pension before the notice is acknowledged.
Requesting a contribution split before lodging the notice.
Claiming in the tax return before the acknowledgement arrives.

items.title: Start a Retirement Phase Flexi Pension
items.when: The member has retired (or met another condition of release) and wants a regular income from super.

steps.do: Check a condition of release is met: 60+ and retired, left a job on or after 60, aged 65+, or stopped work due to permanent incapacity.

source.quote: are aged 65 or over (even if you're still working), or

member.text: {name} is {age}: under 60. Preservation age is 60, so retiring doesn't release their super yet. Retirement Phase is only open if they've stopped work due to permanent incapacity.

steps.do: Check the balance: at least $25,000 is needed to start.

source.quote: You need a minimum of $25,000 to start a Flexi Pension.

steps.do: If only part of the balance is moving, at least $6,000 must stay in super. If all of it moves, insurance stops.

source.quote: If you transfer your entire accumulation account or component to a Retirement Phase Flexi Pension, any existing insurance cover you have will cease.

member.text: {name} has insurance in super. Moving the whole balance ends it.

steps.do: Check the transfer balance cap: $2.1 million for a first retirement pension from 1 July 2026. The member's personal cap comes from the ATO.

source.quote: on or after 1 July 2026 will have a transfer balance cap of $2.1 million

member.text: {name}'s total super balance ({tsb}) is over the cap: not all of it can go into a pension.

steps.do: Bring other super in first: money can't be added to a pension once it starts.

source.quote: Once you start a Flexi Pension, you can't add further amounts to it.

steps.do: Lodge any notice of intent for personal contributions before applying.
Under 60: the member needs an ATO Tax file number declaration for the pension.

source.quote: If you're under age 60, you'll need to complete an ATO Tax file number declaration for each Flexi Pension you start.

member.text: {name} is {age}: a TFN declaration is needed.

steps.do: Retirement Bonus: money must have been in a UniSuper super or TTR account for 12 continuous months before the transfer; the bonus is added when the pension starts. Mention that withdrawing half or more in the first 12 months may claw it back.

source.quote: If you withdraw 50% or more of your opening balance within 12 months of starting your Retirement Phase Flexi Pension, the Trustee may claw back the Retirement Bonus.

steps.do: Agree the set-up: investment options, drawdown order, yearly amount (at least the minimum) and frequency (monthly if none chosen).
Nominations: reversionary beneficiary, binding or non-binding.
Apply: online if they're an Accumulation 1, Accumulation 2 or Personal Account member over 60; otherwise the paper application.

source.quote: Only available for UniSuper Accumulation 1, Accumulation 2 and Personal Account members over age 60.

steps.do: Proof of identity is needed before the pension starts.

source.quote: you'll be required to provide proof of your identity before starting a Flexi Pension

steps.do: Explain what happens next: if there's no active super account to use, a temporary account holds incoming transfers (up to 90 days), the welcome letter confirms the details, and there's a 14-day cooling-off period.

source.quote: You have 14 days from when your Flexi Pension is opened to decide if it's right for you.

mistakes: Starting the pension before other super has arrived (it can't be added later).
Lodging a notice of intent after the pension has started.
Moving the whole balance without mentioning insurance stops.

items.title: Start a TTR Flexi Pension
items.when: The member has reached preservation age, is still working, and wants some income from super.

steps.do: Check preservation age has been reached (it depends on date of birth).

member.text: {name} is {age}, past preservation age ({presAge}).
{name} is {age}: preservation age is {presAge}, so TTR isn't available yet.

steps.do: Check the balance: $25,000 minimum, and at least $6,000 must stay in the accumulation account.

source.quote: You need a minimum of $25,000 to start a TTR Flexi Pension.

steps.do: Lodge any notice of intent before applying.
Explain the limits: a minimum by age, and a maximum of 10% of the balance a year (the maximum isn't pro-rated in the first year).

source.quote: The maximum amount for TTR Flexi Pension isn't subject to the pro-rata rules.

steps.do: Explain lump sums are only available in limited cases while it's a TTR pension.
Explain tax: earnings are taxed up to 15% until it converts to Retirement Phase: automatically at 65, or once the member tells us they've met a condition of release such as retiring.

source.quote: Investment earnings on a TTR Flexi Pension can be subject to tax of up to 15%

steps.do: DBD members: using the defined benefit component ends DBD membership.

member.text: {name} is a DBD member: check which component they're using.

steps.do: Under 60: an ATO TFN declaration is needed.

member.text: {name} is {age}: a TFN declaration is needed.

steps.do: Apply with the paper application: TTR can't be applied for online.

source.quote: Excludes TTR and BIS Flexi Pension applications.

mistakes: Assuming TTR can be applied for online.
Quoting the full 10% maximum as pro-rated.

items.title: Split contributions with a spouse
items.when: The member wants to move some of last year's before-tax contributions to their spouse's super.

steps.do: Confirm they're concessional contributions from last financial year (this year only if the whole balance is leaving).

source.quote: Generally, you can only request a contribution split from contributions made in the previous financial year.

steps.do: Check the spouse: under 60, or 60 to 64 and not retired. Not possible if the spouse is 65 or over.

source.quote: You can't split contributions with your spouse if they're age 65 or over.

member.text: {name}'s spouse is {spouseAge}.

steps.do: Work out the most that can be split: the lesser of 85% of the concessional contributions and the concessional cap.

source.quote: The maximum amount of contributions that can be split each financial year is the lesser of: 85% of your concessional contributions, and the concessional contributions cap applicable to you.

member.text: {name} had {lastCc} of concessional contributions last year: up to {splitMax} can be split.

steps.do: If they're claiming a deduction on any personal contributions, lodge the notice of intent first.
Check the balance stays above $6,000 after the split, or it may be refused.

source.quote: we may refuse the application if it would result in your accumulation balance falling below $6,000

steps.do: Lodge the Contribution splitting form by 30 June. Only one split per financial year.

source.quote: Your concessional contributions can only be split once per financial year.

steps.do: Explain non-concessional contributions, rollovers and co-contributions can't be split.

mistakes: Splitting before the notice of intent is lodged.
Missing the 30 June deadline.

items.title: Make or renew a binding nomination
items.when: The member wants to make, change or renew a binding death benefit nomination.

steps.do: Choose the type: non-lapsing (online or paper, no expiry) or lapsing (paper only, lasts three years).

member.text: {name}'s lapsing nomination was signed {nomSigned} and expires {nomExpires}.

steps.do: Check who's being nominated: only dependants (spouse, children, financial dependants, interdependents) or the legal personal representative.
Allocations must add up to exactly 100%, or the whole nomination is invalid.

source.quote: 100% of your benefit must be allocated (the entire nomination will be invalid if the allocation doesn't equal exactly 100%)

steps.do: Paper form: signed and dated by the member (not a power of attorney) with two witnesses aged 18+ who aren't beneficiaries, both signing the declaration.

source.quote: must be signed and dated by you (not a power of attorney) in the presence of two witnesses, both of whom are over the age of 18 and not nominated to receive the benefit

steps.do: Make sure lapsing or non-lapsing is ticked: an unticked paper form is treated as lapsing.

source.quote: If you don't make a choice when you complete your binding death benefit nomination paper form, your nomination will default to lapsing.

steps.do: Renewing a lapsing nomination: a written notice signed and dated by the member, before it expires.

source.quote: You can do this by providing us with a written notice, signed and dated by you, to that effect.

steps.do: Pension members: a reversionary beneficiary on the pension overrides other nominations for that account.

member.text: {name} has a pension: check whether it has a reversionary beneficiary.

steps.do: Lodge online (non-lapsing) or with the Binding death nomination form. It takes effect once received and accepted.

mistakes: A witness who is also a beneficiary.
Allocations that don't total 100%.
Leaving the lapsing/non-lapsing box blank.

items.title: Lump sum from a Flexi Pension
items.when: A pension member wants an extra amount on top of their regular payments.

steps.do: Check the pension type: a TTR pension only allows lump sums in limited cases.

member.text: {name} has a TTR pension: lump sums are only possible in limited cases.

steps.do: Check the amount: at least $2,000, and enough in the account.

source.quote: You can make lump sum withdrawals of at least $2,000 from your Flexi Pension at any time if you have enough money in your account.

steps.do: Retirement Bonus: taking 50% or more of the opening balance within 12 months of starting may mean the bonus is clawed back.
Explain the yearly minimum isn't reduced by a lump sum.

source.quote: The amount isn't recalculated if you make a withdrawal during the year.

steps.do: Explain tax: tax-free from 60; under 60, taken proportionally from the taxable and tax-free components.

member.text: {name} is {age}: tax may apply to the taxable component.

steps.do: Lodge online (Pension, Flexi withdrawal) or with the Flexi Pension withdrawal form. Proof of identity may be asked for.
Tell the member when to expect it: usually within five business days, into their nominated bank account.

source.quote: Withdrawals are paid into your nominated bank account, usually within five business days of receiving your request.

mistakes: Promising a TTR lump sum without checking the limited circumstances.

items.title: Close a pension or move it back to super
items.when: The member wants to stop their pension and keep the money in super (or, for BIS, take it as cash).

steps.do: Work out whether {{closing-day-count:a pro-rata minimum}} must be paid before it closes this year.

source.quote: However, if you commute or close your Flexi Pension during the year, a minimum income payment (or a pro-rata minimum income payment) may still need to be paid.

steps.do: Retirement Phase or TTR: use the Transfer your Flexi Pension to a super account form, or the member can call.
BIS: the member logs in or calls; the balance is paid as cash.

source.quote: To close your BIS Flexi Pension, log in to your online account or call us.

member.text: {name} has a BIS pension: it's paid out as cash, not to super.

steps.do: Explain where it goes: the rollover strategy, or Balanced if none; a new Accumulation 1 account if they don't have one.

source.quote: If you don't have a rollover strategy, it will be invested in our default Balanced (MySuper) investment option.

mistakes: Forgetting the pro-rata minimum for the year.

items.title: Transfer super to another fund
items.when: The member wants to move all or part of their super to another fund.

steps.do: Lodge any notice of intent first: it can't be accepted after the money leaves.
Lodge any contribution split first: contributions must be split before they're rolled over.

source.quote: Contributions must be split before they are rolled over, transferred, or withdrawn.

steps.do: Check insurance: cover stops when the member leaves UniSuper.

member.text: {name} has insurance with UniSuper: make sure they know it stops.

steps.do: Partial transfer: at least $6,000 must stay, and it's taken pro-rata across investment options.

source.quote: If you're not transferring the entire amount out of your UniSuper account then you must leave at least $6,000 in your account.

steps.do: Up to eight transfer requests in any 12 months.

source.quote: You may request a transfer up to eight times in each 12-month period.

steps.do: Lodge with the Portability and rollover form, or through the new fund.

mistakes: Rolling out before a notice of intent or split is lodged.

items.title: Downsizer contribution
items.when: The member has sold their home and wants to put some of the proceeds into super.

steps.do: Check age: 55 or older.

member.text: {name} is {age}: too young for a downsizer contribution.

steps.do: Check the home was owned for at least 10 years.

source.quote: If you're aged 55 or older and have owned your house for at least 10 years, you may be able to contribute up to $300,000 ($600,000 per couple) into super from the proceeds of selling your home.

steps.do: Amount: up to $300,000 each, from the sale proceeds. Only one home sale can be used.

source.quote: You can only make downsizing contributions for the sale of one home.

steps.do: Send the ATO downsizer form with the payment, generally within 90 days of settlement.
Explain it doesn't count towards the contribution caps, but counts towards the transfer balance cap and the total super balance.
If the ATO rejects it, it may be accepted as a non-concessional contribution, subject to the caps.

source.quote: The ATO may reject your downsizer contribution on eligibility grounds.

mistakes: Paying the contribution without the ATO form.
Missing the 90-day window.

items.title: Insurance has stopped
items.when: The member's insurance cover has stopped and they want it back.

steps.do: Find out why it stopped: no contributions for 16 months, not enough money for premiums, cessation age, or they cancelled it.

member.text: {name} has had no contributions for {monthsInactive} months.

steps.do: If it stopped for low funds or no contributions: apply within 90 days, be under the cessation age and in active employment.

source.quote: apply within 90 days of your cover being stopped

steps.do: Lodge the Insurance cover reinstatement form (or online). It restarts from the date it stopped, at the same level.
To stop it happening again, the member can elect to keep cover.
Past 90 days: they'd need to apply for cover with health evidence.

mistakes: Missing the 90-day restart window.

items.title: Change pension payments or bank account
items.when: A pension member wants to change how much, how often, or where they're paid.

steps.do: Check the new yearly amount is at least the minimum (and no more than 10% for TTR).

member.text: {name}'s minimum this year: {pensionMin}.

steps.do: Frequencies: fortnightly, monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or annual. Payments go out every second Friday (fortnightly) or by the 28th.
Online: Pension payments tab, Your payments. Or the Change of details (pension) or Change of bank account form.

source.quote: Log in to your account and select the `Your payments' option from the `pension payments' tab menu.

steps.do: Credit union accounts can take longer to clear.

source.quote: If your account is held with a credit union, you may not be able to access your income payment on these days

mistakes: Setting an amount below the minimum.

items.title: Early release: severe financial hardship
items.when: The member is under financial pressure and asking to access super early.

steps.do: Check they're receiving eligible Commonwealth income support: it's a condition of this release.

source.quote: You must be receiving eligible government income support benefits to qualify.

steps.do: It's applied for through UniSuper (the Trustee), {{account-path-labels:online}} or with the Financial hardship form.
{{compassionate-examples:Medical treatment, palliative care or mortgage arrears}} instead? That's compassionate grounds, which the member applies for with the ATO.
Explain early access can affect insurance.

member.text: {name} has insurance in super: early access may affect it.

mistakes: Sending compassionate-grounds requests to UniSuper instead of the ATO.
